Mia: Quick RFC follow-up idea — what if our automatic fallback preserves session affinity + a tiny KV cache rehydration so fallbacks don't force full re-generation and huge perf loss?

Raj: Interesting. Main concerns: data isolation + encryption. Per-tenant cache keys would need KMS-wrapped tokens. Also legal for some customers? :thinking_face:

Oliver: Also risk of stale context causing weird outputs. We'd need cache versioning + TTL + safe invalidation path.

Anna: Agree on telemetry. Add a metric `fallback.cache_rehydrate` and `fallback.cache_stale_drop`. That'll help tune TTLs.

Kevin: Implementation sketch: coordinator publishes variant assignment, sidecar tracks `X-Session-Layout` header and derives `cache-key = sha256(tenant|session|variant|version)`. On fallback, sidecar attempts rehydrate before proxying to fallback model. Pseudocode:```
// sidecar rehydrate flow
if (fallback && session && cache.exists(key)) {
  attach(kv_cache)
  routeTo(fallback)
} else {
  routeTo(fallback) // cold path
}
```

Mia: Good. Interface boundaries we should nail in the RFC: controller -> observer (probe) -> sidecar API for rehydrate requests -> coordinator events. Keep the rehydrate API tiny (GET/PUT with version).

Raj: Tradeoffs: increased complexity in the sidecar and more state to manage vs. faster recovery and lower cost during rollbacks. For some model families (stateful LLMs) it's higher risk — maybe opt-in per-model.

Oliver: Edge cases: 1) model architecture change invalidates cache schema 2) global purge needed on bad rollback 3) cross-region sessions — ensure cache replication or just reject rehydrate across regions.

Anna: Ops needs: expose a `cache_rehydrate_hit_rate` dashboard, alerts when stale-drops spike, and a runbook for global purge. Also add a canary for the rehydrate path itself.

Mia: Thoughts on fallback ordering? Prefer: 1) variant-compatible rehydrate 2) lightweight quantized variant 3) CPU-safe golden model. That keeps latency predictable while preserving semantics.

Kevin: Agree. Also suggest a tiny compatibility header `X-Cache-Schema: v12` so sidecars can quickly reject incompatible caches.

Raj: Security: encrypt cache blobs at rest with per-tenant key, and sidecar must never spill plaintext to logs. We'll need an audit for that.

deploy-bot: canary rollout for `service/runner` started (v2026-03-23_14:12) :rocket:

Mia: Action items: I'll draft RFC with proposed API shapes + state machine, include a section for compatibility and purge. Volunteers for reviewers? @Raj @Oliver @Anna @Kevin

Raj: I'll take security + KMS part.

Oliver: I'll write compatibility + invalidation tests.

Anna: I'll add telemetry + runbook snippets.

Kevin: I'll prototype sidecar flow and share a simple crate.

Mia: Great — I'll ping a draft in #architecture by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
